items.title: John Batiste "Bat" Mosley Interview, 1961-09-23
items.q: You take like Jim Wright, now he played for you before I was playing, but he didn't know how to read.

ctx.x: blues and everything else for him to play. Otherwise, he couldn't do anything. Was running on the way back, say from the funeral, like when they have, didn't they ramble and some of the... Well, they played out, yeah. They played ramble. Did they know any of the other jazz tunes or Dixieland, what they call Dixieland tunes? Yeah, they knew all the head numbers like that. They had those head numbers.

Yeah, they had them like that. Yeah, they played out. So like them. They knew ramble and different things like that. All those old numbers like that. They wouldn't know them. So they didn't... You take the musicians during that time, well you take during that time outside playing street music like that, the fellas playing like dance music, didn't know anything but reading.
